checked_decisions.finding: Motto ruling. 1711 is a verbatim quotation of the series motto (nedaru na, kachitore, sasureba ataeraren) and keeps the official English dub wording. 1698-1700 are NOT a quotation: they are the boy's own paraphrase, adding 'waiting won't do' (absent from the motto) and recasting the motto's two verbs nedaru / kachitoru in first person. Because the same two verbs are deliberately echoed and 1711 then recites the motto in reaction, the echo was made audible in English with the dub's key phrases ('beg for things', 'do it myself') while keeping the rows' own sentence structure; 1698 has no motto counterpart and is unchanged.
Ruri continuation pair; 'Harry' nickname follows the earlier researched decision; Scub Coral is the official term.
Talho/Holland bickering: addressees and tone correct; 1672 'otosu' covers losing the ship, 'doesn't get shot down' is acceptable.

Izumo bridge exchange: Jurgens orders reinforcements, Dominic objects as Intelligence, Jurgens asserts Air Force command priority, Dominic mutters 'zokubutsu'. Names match glossary; 'Intelligence' for jouhou-bu accepted.
Shagia offers to take over, Jurgens refuses then grudgingly thanks him. 1687 fragment kept as a fragment. 1689 read as an order to the ship, which the imperative 'junbi da' supports.
Younger brother questions, elder explains the favor; 'them' keeps the debtor open.
Approach of the boy on the ref board: no name and no pronoun for him beyond 'son'/'kid', both stated in source.
Tutorial warnings about the ranged-combat enemy machine preserved in full, including close-the-distance advice and evasion priority.
Enemy ace taunts and the GX pilot's retort: machine-versus-pilot contrast preserved; no names added.
<on()>/<off()> event lines: commands intact, interjections kept neutral, 1741-1742 '14 years' preserved, 1745 identical to 1701.

uncertainties.issue: The English dub itself has more than one wording of the motto (a short 'Don't beg for it, earn it!' is also attested for Holland). The three-clause source matches the long dub form, so that form was kept; note the dub's last clause ('or else you won't get anything') inverts the Japanese 'and it shall be given'. Official wording wins per project rule.

The official dub wording of this specific episode-2 line could not be retrieved, so these rows are aligned to the dub motto's key phrases rather than to an official rendering of the line itself. 1700 now says 'do it myself' where the Japanese says 'go and win it'; this follows the dub's own equation kachitore = 'do it yourself'. Revert 1700 to 'win it myself' if the orchestrator prefers literal over echo.

Fix is an idiom call: the literal draft was not a mistranslation word-for-word, but its English sense (custody) differs from the source's sarcastic thanks. 'The other day' implies an earlier encounter with the younger brother; rows 261+ probably belong to a later/alternate encounter than rows 131-137, as the translator noted.
